prove:mixedbase.summary:
This round settled 20 new mixed-base systems. Every proof is exact and has a check script; all five check scripts exit 0, and the slowest takes under 20 s.

**Tools.** mixedlib.py is a descent-certificate engine for maps whose modulus has several prime factors, with an independent verifier. pairlib.py is a run-accelerated engine for the Farkas pairing family; "tail leaves" let it handle unbounded up-runs. lemmas.md restates the round-2 lemmas for several primes, with full proofs:
- A' (certificate gives GLOBAL plus the cycle list);
- B' (an expanding periodic point rules out any certificate);
- C' (the engine terminates exactly when a certificate exists);
- R (an unbounded uncaught run rules out any certificate);
- D'' (fixed points of words when some primes expand and others contract).

**Pairing family P(a, K, x*), with m = a^K.**
- A closed-form block lemma holds for the whole family.
- GLOBAL on all integers is proved for K = 1 (every odd a, every x*) and for (a, K) = (3, 2).
- No plain certificate exists for any member.
- An exact obstruction rules out every certificate, even run-accelerated, in all remaining cases. So the closed form reaches exactly K = 1 and (3, 2), and P(3,3,±1), P(5,2,±1), P(7,2,±1) are the first open members.
- The new settled system mb_pair_3_9m is 3x+1 tamed by one class of density 1/9 that no certificate can handle.

**Single taming classes (complete classifications).**
- 3x+1: a certificate exists only for n ≡ 2 (mod 3) and n ≡ 8 (mod 9) → (n+1)/m. Necessity holds for every constant c.
- 5x+1: only n ≡ 3 (mod 5).
- 7x+1: only n ≡ 4 (mod 7), proved for odd m ≤ 199.
- The mechanism the task proposed (the run passes through every residue mod m) does occur, but it is proved never to be enough for a single class: the run grows by (a/2)^(m−1)/m > 1, which yields an expanding periodic point.

**Sparse multi-class tamings (certified, with proved minimality).**
- 3x+1 at densities 2/27, 3/81, 4/243 and 7/729. The minimum number of classes mod 3^K for K = 2..6 is exactly 1, 2, 3, 4, 7.
- 5x+1 at 2/25 and 4/125.
- 7x+1 at 2/49 and 5/343.

**Relatives of the open entries.**
- div23_5n1 plus one class: the complete list of classes that can admit a certificate is proved. All but one unresolved pair (n ≡ 2 mod 4, plus the trivial even class, which is the open map itself) are certified, and the sparsest is n ≡ 26 (mod 30) → (n+4)/30, density 1/30. A sparse 2-adic version, n ≡ 7 (mod 8) → (n+1)/8, needs a certificate with 93 leaves and depth 24.
- m3_b plus at most two classes: the classes must be ±1 mod q with q in {2, 3, 4, 6, 8}, all certified. The sparsest is ±1 mod 8 (density 1/4).

**Not done.** z3 and pysat are not installed, so no solver search for matrix interpretations was run. Linear residue-weighted potentials are proved impossible for every open system. Novelty was not checked by web search; only the K = 1, a = 3 pairing case is known (Farkas 2005).

- **First open single-class tamings of 3x+1** (density 1/27):
  - mb_s3_27: n ≡ 26 (mod 27) → (n+1)/27; else even → n/2; else (3n+1)/2.
  - mb_pair_3_27m: n ≡ 13 (mod 27) → (n−13)/27; else even → n/2; else (3n+1)/2, on the nonnegative integers.
  - The negative 3x+1 cycle (−5 −7 −10) blocks every descent-type certificate for both, run-accelerated ones included. Both converge for every start below 10^6 (evidence only).
- **Open pairing-family members:** P(3,3,±1), P(5,2,±1) and P(7,2,±1), for example mb_pair_5_25p, which has the real cycle (3 6). The heuristic predicts convergence for a = 3 at every K and divergence for a = 7 at K ≥ 4.
- **Unproved trend:** that 3x+1 needs only a vanishing fraction of classes mod 3^K for every K. The proved minima are 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 for K = 2..6.
- **Unresolved by both methods:** div23_5n1 plus n ≡ 2 (mod 4) → (n+2)/4.
- **Not searched:** m3_b with three or more classes.
- **7x+1 single class:** a uniform proof for m > 199 was not written.

theorems.statement: For P(a,K,x*) with m=a^K, r=x*/2 mod m, c=(m-1)x*/2, b=(2-a)x*: for odd n not = r mod m and n != x*, with n-x*=2^j u and j=qK+l, T^(j+1+q)(n)=(x*+a^l u)/2. For K=1 (every odd a>=3) and for (a,K)=(3,2), every integer orbit is eventually periodic, and every cycle meets |n|<=5|x*| (|n|<=|x*| when K=1). Cycle lists are computed for all |x*|<=43.

theorems.statement: No family member admits a plain descent certificate, because x* is an expanding fixed point (multiplier a/2). For a>=5, K>=2 the 2-cycle {y,2y} with y=(2-a)x*/(4-a) (multiplier a/4) rules out run-accelerated certificates too; for a=3, K>=3 the cycle {5x*,7x*,10x*} (multiplier 9/8) does the same.

theorems.statement: For odd m<=199, a certificate exists only for (m,r)=(7,4). It is certified, and every orbit reaches (1 4).

theorems.statement: Minimum number of classes mod m for which a certificate exists: 3x+1 mod 27/81/243/729 = 2/3/4/7; 5x+1 mod 25/125 = 2/4; 7x+1 mod 49/343 = 2/5. theorems.statement: Any (q,r) for which div23_5n1 plus one class n=r mod q -> (n+c)/q admits a certificate is in an explicit list with q<=30. This holds for every c and for either priority, because the class must catch the cycles (-1 -4 -2) and -42/13, which forces q<=45. All listed pairs are certified except the trivial even class (the open map itself) and the pair n = 2 mod 4, which is unresolved. The sparsest is n=26 mod 30 -> (n+4)/30, with every orbit reaching (1 6 3).

prove:accel.summary:
I classified all 12 OBST S-family systems, but none is settled: 4 turn out to be the 3x+1 problem and 8 are new open problems. I did settle five new OBST systems: acc_h32 and acc_h16 need a real machine-verified proof, while acc_h9, dress_23_x1 and dress_32_x1 are easy and labelled as such. Three checks exit 0: check_trichotomy.py (~15 s), check_sfamily.py (~45 s), check_dressing.py (~5 s). No literature search was done, so every novelty claim is "not checked".

**The 12 OBST S-family systems (m = 2, 3)**
- Two are literally 3x+1: S = all odd classes for m = 2 and for m = 3.
- Two more are 3x+1 in disguise. For S = {n ≡ 3 mod 4} there is an exact conjugacy with z = (n−1)/2: T_S^2(2z+1) = 2T(z)+1, where T is the 3x+1 map (Theorem Z / Corollary C).
- The other 8 are written out as explicit maps in z. Proved for each: no descent certificate, no accelerated certificate (Theorem N below), and the exact list of cycles of period ≤ 26.
- One of them, W (S = {1,3,7} mod 8), has positive drift (+0.046 per odd step), so its real question is whether some orbit diverges. The orbit of n = 15 passes 10^60 (evidence only).

**General theorems, all proved, for maps whose multipliers are p-adic units (a residue graph at level p^K records which classes can follow which):**
- **Theorem H:** if every strongly connected component (SCC) of that graph is either contracting or a single simple expanding cycle, then every orbit is eventually periodic and the cycle list is a finite computation. The proof uses a weighted potential on each component, with weights verified exactly.
- **Theorem N (the barrier):** if an expanding cycle shares its component with another cycle ("free re-entry"), there are infinitely many expanding periodic orbits piling up at the expanding point. So no certificate that accelerates along finitely many orbits with locally constant stopping times can exist, including classes with a symbolic run exponent.
- **Theorem T:** the two combine into an exact boundary: an accelerated certificate exists if and only if no expanding cycle shares its component with another cycle. This does not depend on the level chosen.
- **Theorem K ("dressing"):** replace x/p by q^e·x/p on p-divisible numbers and add x/q on q-divisible ones. The result has the same first-return map, so the same answer and cycles, but never a descent certificate. This shows the unit-multiplier condition in Theorem N is necessary.

Computed applications:
- In the S-family there is no system with an isolated expanding cycle for any m ≤ 5 (exhaustive, exact). So all 2 + 10 + 172 + 48880 OBST members are blocked by Theorem N.
- Exact barrier witnesses are checked for 3x+1, 5x+1, split5_1, split5_3, m3_e, perm_1932, desc_m3_4n5 and desc_split7_1.
- A scan of the catalog found no open system that Theorem H would settle.

**Systems settled:**
- **acc_h32:** 3n+1 on 11 of the 16 odd classes mod 32, with n+1 or n+9 patches on the rest. Cycles (1 4 2), (3 10 5 6), (19 58 29 38).
- **acc_h16:** cycles (1 4 2), (3 10 5 6).
- **acc_h9:** base 3; fixed points 1, 4, 7.
- **dress_23_x1:** only cycle (1 2 3).
- **dress_32_x1:** only cycle (1 2).
- I also proved dress_23_3x1 equivalent to 3x+1 and dress_23_5x1 equivalent to the catalog problem div23_5n1. Both stay open.

The settled H examples were found by computer search, so they are constructed rather than natural systems.
prove:accel.open_frontier:
- **The 8 new S-family cores stay open (tier 5).** Theorem N rules out every accelerated or local certificate for them. A proof would need non-local information: either a conjugacy (I found none between any core and 3x+1 or each other), or orbit statistics that limit how often an orbit can return deep into the expanding region.
- **Core W (S = {1,3,7} mod 8) is expected to be divergent.** Its sharp question is whether some orbit diverges, e.g. z = 7 (n = 15). Proving that would need a provably divergent orbit, which is as hard as for 5x+1.
- **The S-family barrier is only checked for m ≤ 5.** Whether the S-family never has an isolated expanding cycle for any m is unproved beyond that.
- **Theorem H settles no open catalog system.** The scan found none of the right shape.
- **Literature novelty was not checked** for any of the results.

theorems.name: Theorem H (isolated expanding cycles are harmless)
theorems.statement: For a unit-multiplier p-adic residue-class system with no division-free cycle: if every SCC of the cylinder graph G_K is contracting or a single simple cycle, then every positive orbit is eventually periodic. The complete cycle list comes from a finite computation: an SCC-wise weighted potential with exactly verified rational weights, plus the type-(b) periodic points that are positive integers.

theorems.name: Theorem N (acceleration barrier)
theorems.statement: If an expanding cycle C lies in an SCC of G_K that contains another cycle (free re-entry), then the closed walks C^d W give infinitely many expanding periodic orbits accumulating at x*. Hence no generalized certificate exists: no countable cylinder cover of Z_p minus finitely many periodic orbits with locally constant stopping times. This includes accelerated certificates with a symbolic run exponent and bounded lookahead.

theorems.name: Theorem T (trichotomy, level independence)
theorems.statement: For unit-multiplier systems with no division-free cycle: (1) a plain certificate exists iff all SCCs are contracting; (2) a generalized certificate exists iff no SCC contains an expanding cycle together with another cycle; (3) in case (2), GLOBAL holds with computable cycles. The SCC type of an expanding orbit is the same at every level K.

theorems.name: S-family barrier (m<=5)
theorems.statement: For every subset S at m = 2..5, no SCC of G_m is an expanding simple cycle. So all 2+10+172+48880 OBST members of the S-family admit no generalized (accelerated) certificate.

theorems.name: Catalog barrier witnesses
theorems.statement: 3x+1, 5x+1, split5_1, split5_3, m3_e, perm_1932, desc_m3_4n5 and desc_split7_1 have explicit exact Theorem-N witnesses y_d (d <= 24), so none of them admits a generalized certificate.

theorems.name: Theorem Z (half-shift conjugacy for the S-family)
theorems.statement: For odd n = 2z+1, the next odd value of the T_S-orbit equals 2G_S(z)+1, where G_S(z) = (odd(3z+2)-1)/2 if n mod 2^m is in S, and (odd(z+1)-1)/2 otherwise.

theorems.name: Corollary C (S = {3 mod 4} is 3x+1)
theorems.statement: For S = {n = 3 mod 4}, T_S^2(2z+1) = 2T(z)+1 with T the 3x+1 map. So sf2_3 and sf3_37 are exactly equivalent to the 3x+1 problem, with cycles (1 2) and (3 10 5 6) corresponding to z = 0 and the 3x+1 cycle (1 2).

theorems.name: Theorem K (dressing)
theorems.statement: For primes p != q and q^e > p, the dressed map D (p|x -> q^e x/p; else q|x -> x/q; else g) and the undressed map U (p|x -> x/p; q|x -> x/q; else g) have the same first-return map rho(g(w)) on pq-rough numbers. So GLOBAL(D) iff GLOBAL(U), with cycles in bijection, yet D never has a descent certificate. Hence the unit-multiplier hypothesis of Theorem N is necessary.

theorems.name: Exact short-cycle lists for the 12 S-family OBST systems
theorems.statement: Every T_S-cycle of period <= 26 is listed exactly for each of the 12 systems, by enumerating all closed walks. For sf3_137 they are (1 4 2), (3 10 5 6), a 9-cycle through 7 and a 15-cycle through 39. Extending to period 30 gives the same lists (scratch/cycles30.py).

prove:deep.summary:
GLOBAL is still open for both split5_3 = SPLIT(5,1,3) and split5_1 = SPLIT(5,1,1). split5_3_deep.md section 6 records what blocks each lens idea: (a) no well-founded order or conjugacy was found; (b) the rising family 4^K-3 reduces to an open question about the binary digits of 5^K; (c) by round 2's two-sided theorem, no bounded-depth search for smaller ancestors can exclude more than 1/4 of the candidates; (d) the set of 2-adic points that never descend (Omega) is fully described, with its dimension computed exactly.

What was settled:
(1) The family SPLIT(a,b,d) (n=1 mod 4 -> an+d, n=3 mod 4 -> bn+d) is classified. Each member falls in exactly one class:
- P: parity map (a=b).
- C: settled by descent.
- D: provably divergent. Every odd value strictly increases, so there are no cycles. Easy.
- K: exactly conjugate to an accelerated parity map. SPLIT(1,3,1) is the 3x+1 map; split_3 = SPLIT(3,1,3) is equivalent to Collatz no-divergence. So swapping 5 back to 3 in the d=3 column already gives a Collatz-hard problem.
- R: reduces to a smaller-d member.
- O: open.
The 128-member table (a,b<=7, d<=15) splits as P 32 / C 8 / K 16 / D 16 / R 8 / O 48.

(2) BASIN (which cycle each start reaches) is solved for two infinite families of settled maps:
- X_d = SPLIT(1,1,d), every odd d: cycles correspond exactly to cosets of <2> mod d, with explicit elements, and the basin of n is its coset.
- Sigma_d (split_d / splitB_d) with gcd(d,6)=1: every merging class meets every compatible arithmetic progression. Consequently a cycle's basin is a congruence set exactly when it is alone in its <2,3>-class mod d; otherwise the basin is not ultimately periodic and not automatic in any base.
This settles BASIN for 7 catalog systems: split_5, split_73, split_97, splitB_7 and splitB_71 have congruence basins; split_13 (cycles 1 and 5) and split_7081 (cycles 569 and 713) have shared classes with nonautomatic basins.

(3) Exact Hausdorff dimension of Omega for every split map: dim = log2 of the minimum over theta of a 2x2 transfer-matrix spectral radius, in closed form H_2(1-2/log2 c) for the type containing split5_3.
- split5_3: 0.5806841 exactly.
- split5_1: certified in [0.936275, 0.936852]. This gap explains why earlier methods went much further on split5_3.
- Members with positive drift have Omega of positive Haar measure.
- The number of starts n <= X that never fall below themselves is O(X^dim).
- On multiples of 3, split5_3 is conjugate to the new open map SPLIT(1,5,1).

All three check scripts (check_family.py, check_basins.py, check_omega.py) exit 0 in under 10 s each. They use exact arithmetic, and the accessibility proof is run constructively on 72 random targets. Literature novelty was not checked (no web search).

prove:density.summary:
This round proves density theorems for 38 open catalog maps but settles no open GLOBAL question, and it adds no new systems. What it does is turn round 2's case-by-case "never-dropping starts" bounds into one general method, with a tool that issues exact certificates for any residue-table map (density_lib.py, make_certificates.py). The method builds an adaptive digit tree on a finite state graph; mixed-prime maps like div23 and div235 split by 2, 3 or 5 as needed.

Main results, all with written proofs in theory.md:
- **Thm 1:** an exact inequality N_{s,γ}w ≤ w gives H(X) ≤ 2^{k0} + C1·X^{1−γ}, with explicit constants.
- **Thm 2:** the best exponent is θ* = 1 − sup_{s>0} γ*(s), and θ* < 1 exactly when the drift is negative.
- **Thm 3:** under a hypothesis (H), θ* is the exact limit of this method (standard tilting argument).
- **Thm 4 (Korec-type):** for every c > c0 = 1 + Δ/Λ, almost every n has an iterate below n^c. For 3x+1 this recovers Korec's log_4 3 and the Terras exponent H(log_3 2) = 0.94996 as a sanity check.
- **Prop 4.2:** c0 is sharp for the method.
- **Thm 5:** for expanding maps, almost every orbit rises above n^c for every c < c0. This covers 5x+1, 7x+1, 9x+1 and the 1932 permutation family.
- **Thm 6:** the set of starts that drop below themselves within log_p n tree steps has exact density q. For 5x+1, q is in [0.82378, 0.82407]; for 7x+1 q ≈ 0.699249; for 9x+1 q ≈ 0.613870.
- **Prop 7:** showing the full drop set has density < 1 would already prove a divergent orbit or infinitely many cycles, so that question is out of reach here.

Certified never-drop exponents θ: div235 0.93866, div23_5n1 0.85958, div23_7n1 0.99900, m3_b/m3_d 0.96481, m3_g 0.99948, the 3n+d family 0.94996, split5_1 0.93685 (was 0.9383), split5_3 0.58069 (was 0.58496), desc_m3_4n5 0.74870, desc_s32_plus9 0.56976, desc_split7_1 0.75348 (was 0.75488).

Checks:
- check_density.py exits 0 (ALL CHECKS PASSED). It takes about 3.5 minutes, over the 2-minute target.
- check_hypH.py exits 0 in a few seconds.
- evidence.py is numerical only (labelled EVIDENCE). It shows that in [2^17, 2^18) the share of 5x+1 starts that drop at all is about q. That suggests the conjecture that the full drop set has density exactly q.

Literature: Korec's threshold was confirmed through Tao's paper (arXiv:1909.03562). Terras, Venturini and Matthews–Watts are cited from memory and not re-read; novelty is otherwise not checked.
prove:density.open_frontier:
- Every GLOBAL question listed is still open (tier 5).
- Theorem 3 and Prop 4.2 prove that the depth-log n tree cannot beat θ* or c0, so a Tao-type argument would be needed for "almost every orbit reaches a known cycle". Iterating Theorem 4 fails.
- Expanding maps: whether the full drop set has density exactly q. The evidence says yes, but by Prop 7 any upper bound below 1 implies a divergent orbit or infinitely many cycles.
- Hypothesis (H), second half (an interior minimiser), is checked only numerically; it is used only in the optimality theorem.
- That θ* does not depend on the split order for mixed-prime maps is evidence only.
- The true exponent of H(X) is far below θ* (conjecturally the count is O(1)).
- The early-drop density q is not computed for maps with signed intercepts (the permutations); only the lower bound holds there.

prove:traps.summary:
I built a complete decision procedure for when a residue trap statement can be proved by residue methods. The statement is S(T,A): every positive orbit of T (3x+1, 5x+1, 7x+1, or any map of the form n/2 | a n + b) meets the residue set A mod 2^k, or ends in an explicit list of cycles. The procedure has proofs on both sides and settles 490 new systems with certificates. `check.py` runs every check in about 10–15 s and exits 0.

**Decision procedure (theory.md, all proved).** It looks only at the residue graph mod 2^k with A removed. Every trap set falls into exactly one of three cases, decided at that single level:
- **P0** (Theorem 1): every cycle of the graph contracts. Then an exact integer potential exists, every untrapped orbit drops into [1, B], and a finite simulation finishes the proof. This is equivalent to a descent certificate existing.
- **P1** (Theorem 2): some expanding cycles exist, but each one is isolated as a simple cycle (for example the runs near −1 for 3x+1, −1/3 for 5x+1, −1/5 for 7x+1). The statement is still proved. This answers task item (4): provable despite an expanding cycle.
- **H** (Theorems 3–4): the graph contains a homoclinic orbit — a point that leaves an expanding 2-adic periodic point and returns to it without hitting A. Then no residue-graph, SCC or descent certificate exists at any modulus. Theorem 4 builds the witness explicitly whenever the level-k test fails, so nothing is left undecided.
- `verify.py` checks every certificate independently: it rebuilds the graph by brute force and tests only the conditions the proof uses.

**Agreement with the YAH table.** For 3x+1 on subsets of Z/8 the result is: A is provable iff A ⊄ {1} and A ⊄ {0,5,7}. This matches the proved/open table of Yolcu–Aaronson–Heule on every set they list. Their $500 open sets {0}, {1}, {5}, {7}, {5,7} are all H, with explicit witnesses (for example x* = −20, multiplier 9/8, z = −28 for {7}).

**Census (census.md).** I classified all 2^16 sets for each of:
- 3x+1, 5x+1, 7x+1 with all residues mod 8 and mod 16;
- the same three maps with odd residues mod 32.

The frontier (sets that are H but become provable by adding any one residue) has 130 sets in total. YAH Conjecture 4.14 ({5,7} mod 8) lifts into exactly one of them mod 16: F* = {0,3,5,7,8,10,13,14,15}. That is the weakest mod-16 weakening of the conjecture that no residue method reaches. Adding any of 1, 2, 4, 6, 9, 11, 12 makes it provable. For 5x+1 and 7x+1, every minimal provable set mod 32 needs Theorem 2; none is P0. The smallest provable odd trap sets for 3x+1 mod 2^k have sizes 1, 2, 3, 4 for k = 3..6 (proved by exact branch and bound). The k = 7 search did not finish within the compute budget, so whether the trend continues to density 0 is open.

**Families (Theorem F, family.md).** If the graph has only trivial and simple components, the statement holds for every map in the congruence class at once. Examples:

theorems.name: Lemma 0 (walk lifting)
theorems.statement: A walk in the avoider graph G_m^A with E halvings lifts to a cylinder of level m+E, and T^l maps that cylinder affinely onto the end cylinder. A closed walk has a unique rational periodic lift with the cycle's multiplier, and it is the only 2-adic point whose residue path is that cycle repeated forever.

theorems.name: Theorem 1 (pure potential dichotomy)
theorems.statement: The following are equivalent: all cycles of G_{m0}^A contract; all cycles contract at every level; no expanding periodic avoider exists; an avoider descent certificate exists. When they hold, an exact integer potential phi gives V(n) = n 2^{phi/Q}, which strictly decreases above an explicit B, so every avoiding orbit enters [1,B].
theorems.novelty: close to YAH (arXiv:2105.14697) Prop 4.7 residue-graph ranking, as transcribed in census/round2/literature; not re-read

theorems.name: Theorem 2 (SCC certificate with isolated expanding cycles)
theorems.statement: If every SCC of G_m^A is trivial, a simple cycle, or contracting, then every positive orbit meets A, enters [1,B], or equals a positive-integer lift of a simple cycle. So S(T,A) holds with an explicit cycle list, even when expanding 2-adic cycles exist.

theorems.name: Theorem 3 (homoclinic obstruction)
theorems.statement: If an expanding periodic avoider x* has a homoclinic avoider orbit (z congruent to x* mod 2^{m0}, z not on the orbit of x*, T^j z = x*), then at every level m the SCC of x* is non-simple and non-contracting. Hence no SCC certificate and no descent certificate exists at any modulus.

theorems.name: Theorem 4 (non-simple expanding SCC gives a homoclinic orbit)
theorems.statement: A non-simple SCC containing an expanding cycle, at any level, yields an explicit homoclinic avoider orbit. The construction is used in the census and verified exactly in every H case.

theorems.name: Corollary 5 and Lemma 6 (decision procedure)
theorems.statement: The Theorem-2 hypothesis holds at some level iff it holds at level m0 = max(k,beta) iff no homoclinic orbit exists. Every trap set is exactly one of P0, P1 or H, and provability is monotone in A. For 3x+1 on Z/8: A is provable iff A is not contained in {1} or in {0,5,7}, which agrees with the YAH proved/open table on every set they list.

theorems.name: Census theorem (complete classification)
theorems.statement: Every trap set in nine censuses is classified with a verified certificate or a verified homoclinic witness, with no set undecided: 3x+1, 5x+1, 7x+1 for all residues mod 8 and mod 16 and odd residues mod 32. There are 490 minimal provable sets and 130 maximal H sets. YAH Conjecture 4.14 lifts into the unique mod-16 frontier set F* = {0,3,5,7,8,10,13,14,15}.

theorems.name: Minimum provable odd trap size
theorems.statement: The minimum size of a provable set of odd residues mod 2^k for 3x+1 is 1, 2, 3, 4 for k = 3, 4, 5, 6, by exact branch and bound on witness sets. Continuation to density 0 is not established.

theorems.name: Theorem F (uniform families)
theorems.statement: If G_k^A for C_{a0,b0} has only trivial and simple SCCs, then for all odd a, b >= 1 congruent to (a0, b0) mod 2^k every positive orbit meets A or ends in an explicit positive-integer lift, and such lifts exist only when a^o < 2^E. Corollaries: every trajectory of n/2 | an+b with a >= 3 contains a term congruent to 4 mod 8. For a >= 5 two odd trap pairs mod 8 per class work with no exceptions. For a >= 9 six sets mod 16 per class work.
theorems.novelty: a=3, b=1, A={4} is YAH-proved; the general families have novelty not checked

theorems.name: Theorem E (density bound for trap avoiders)
theorems.statement: For the shortcut map T_{a,b} and a trap set A, the number of n <= X avoiding A is at most 2 (sum v / min v) lambda^{floor(log2 X) - k} = O(X^{log2 lambda}), for any exact Perron certificate M v <= lambda v. It reproduces the exponents 0.4057 and 0.8792 for {5,7} and {7} mod 8. The 3x+1 frontier sets mod 32 have exponents in [0.223, 0.613].

prove:dichotomy.summary:
I proved a general dichotomy theorem for table maps T(n)=(u_r n+v_r)/w_r on any modulus Q, mixed moduli included. The hypotheses are gcd(u_r,Q)=1, w_r | Q with exact division, and positivity. Under them, a descent certificate exists if and only if every cycle of the residue graph contracts, and equivalently if an integer one-step potential exists. The critical case (multiplier exactly 1) turns out to be exactly translation cycles, and these always block a certificate. The obstruction proof needs no periodic point, which is what makes it work for mixed moduli. I also proved that certificate depth k* has an exact formula on the graph, gave explicit exceptional sets, and gave a counterexample showing the gcd hypothesis is necessary.

decide.py turns this into a decision procedure: it always answers CERT or OBST, with no UNKNOWN case, and every answer is re-checked in exact arithmetic. A CERT answer includes the complete cycle list and k*.

Applications:
- **New settled systems:** 17 new systems are settled with complete cycle lists, plus one where every orbit diverges.
- **Depth records:** the deepest is k*=2466 at modulus 27, driven by a near-critical 80/81 cycle; the round-2 record was 44. Others are 655 at modulus 81 and 332 for a 3n+1/n+1 table mod 64. All of these also have one-step potential proofs, so depth measures the certificate format rather than difficulty.
- **Phase diagrams:** exhaustive exact counts for B(9,a), B(27,a) (2.1M tables, 76,452 certifiable), C9 (262,144 tables) and mixed D(36,a).
- **Open entries:** all 34 open GLOBAL table maps are proved OBST, so no plain descent proof of any of them exists at any modulus. 1330 one- and two-class neighbours at the next modulus are certifiable, and a new invariant, distance to provability, is tabulated for each entry.
- **3x+1:** I proved that its distance to provability grows exponentially in the number of classes; exact values are 1,1,1,2,2,4,5,8 for m=1..8.

All four check scripts exit 0: check_dichotomy.py (about 1.5 min), check_systems.py (about 5 s), check_phase.py (about 25 s) and check_neighbours.py (about 25 s).

On novelty: the residue Markov chain goes back to Matthews–Watts (1984/85). I did not find the deterministic dichotomy in one web search, and novelty is otherwise not checked.
prove:dichotomy.open_frontier:
Open questions:
- Does dist_{2^m}(3x+1)/2^m tend to 0? The values decrease monotonically up to m=8, but this is evidence only.
- Do the permutation entries (perm_1932, perm_b, perm_swap, perm_c, perm_d) need a positive power of the modulus in modified classes? The pattern 4·2^{k-2} at modulus 3^k suggests so; a measure-preservation argument is plausible but unproved.
- Is k* unbounded in B(3^k,2) and C(3^k) without translation chains, via near-critical cycles 2^a5^b/3^c -> 1? This is conjectured, not proved.
- Is there a sharp threshold in the multiplier a for family B(Q,a)? There is a drop between a=8 and a=10.
- Many distance values are only bracketed at Q' >= 81 because the hitting-set search timed out.
- For the open entries themselves, the dichotomy only proves that plain descent certificates cannot settle them.

prove:divergence.summary:
I settled six new systems with provably infinite orbits and proved five general theorems. All seven check scripts pass via check.py (about 70 s).

Answer to task (1):
- Theorem 1: for every b-suffix map, including non-injective ones, the fate of a seed is decidable. Every infinite orbit has a pump and a congruence-plus-finite certificate with no periodic points, so automata never beat congruences in that class.
- Theorem 2: for a b-automatic set C, the sequence C/b^a is eventually periodic. A family of forced-in and forced-out points therefore rules out automatic certificates of every size.

Two certificate tools:
- Theorem 3 (ascent traps for non-injective maps): a forward-closed union of residue classes whose cycles all have slope product > 1 contains no periodic point. Its companion lemmas prove infinitely many falls and that the orbit's sequence of residue classes is not eventually periodic (so there is no affine pump). Each comes with an exact integer witness.
- Theorem 4 (precision lemma for 2-adic maps): any congruence trap at any modulus 2^K contains a trap at the map's own modulus 2^m. This gives a finite test that rules out congruence certificates at every modulus.

Task (2) systems:
- race_s21 (non-injective, counter-machine type): GLOBAL settled — the cycles are exactly the fixed points coprime to 30, and n diverges iff v2(n) < v3(n) + v5(n). A 2-state base-6 automaton is a certificate (minimum size 2). No base-2^j or base-3^j automaton of any size works, and no congruence certificate exists at any modulus.
- fx10_64_s7 and fx26_32_s7 (5x+1 with one class changed): fixed sets of 6 residue classes diverge entirely, with infinitely many falls and non-periodic itineraries, and the orbit of 7 enters them.
- perm12_s7: a new permutation whose orbit of 7 is infinite, via a separator mod 12 (least possible), with forced falls.
- swT2_8_s8: a new two-swap neighbour of the 1932 map whose orbit of 8 is infinite. The least separator modulus of the form 2^i·3^j is exactly 2304.
- c62_64_s27: accelerated 3x+1 (contracting on average) with one class changed. The orbit of 27 is provably infinite and non-monotone, but only by a tier-1 affine pump.

Task (3):
- 5x+1: the finest change that settles a non-monotone orbit of 7 has density 1/64 (fx10_64_s7). At moduli 128 and 256, the precision lemma proves that 17576 of 18048 single-class changes in the family admit no congruence certificate at any modulus. The remaining 172 at modulus 128 give only monotone traps for 7, checked up to modulus 2^11 (evidence only).
- 1932 map: Theorem 5 (mixed 2·3-adic precision lemma) reduces separators at any modulus 2^i·3^j to a finite graph mod 2^i·9. It excludes congruence separators at every modulus 2^i·3^j with i ≤ 18 for swT9 (CLS-055), G itself, {3}, {3,9} and {3,15}. Among 138 swap sets mod 18, the same test finds only {9,15} (round 2's result), {2,8} (new) and {7,10} (orbit looks monotone).
- SAT search found no automaton separator for swT9 with up to 8–9 states in bases 2, 3, 6 and 12 (evidence only).

Caveats:
- Nothing has been refereed.
- Literature novelty was not checked for anything.
- pysat is not installed system-wide. The SAT results were run from a private venv, and no check script depends on them.

prove:polynomial.summary:
Round 3 settles 17 polynomial Collatz systems over F_2, F_3 and F_4, plus two infinite families with one or more members for every k ≥ 1. It proves three general theorems (A, B, C) and the renormalization lemmas behind every divergence proof. One central question stays open: g = 1+t+t^2 with h = 1 over F_2 (Nichols 2016).

All maps have the form T(f) = f/t if f(0) = 0, else (g f - g(0) f(0) h)/t. Running `python3 check.py` runs the five check scripts; each exits 0, about 40 s in total. All arithmetic is exact.

**General theorems**
- **Theorem A (F_2, g = 1+t, every twist h):** every orbit is eventually periodic. With h = (1+t)^a k, the class mod k is invariant, and a nonzero f reaches {0, h} exactly when k divides f. If (1+t) does not divide h, the basin of the fixed point h is exactly the nonzero multiples of h. The only cycles are {0} and {h} exactly when h is a power of (1+t). This generalizes HMYZ 2008.
- **Theorem B (every degree-1 multiplier over every F_q, twists (g/g0)^a):** f is periodic exactly when its Newton sequence never vanishes. Periodic points of degree below p^e correspond one-to-one with nowhere-zero words of length p^e, (q-1)^{p^e} of them, and T acts as the shift. This classifies all cycles of the Snapp–Tracy maps, which their paper only exhibited.
- **Theorem C (Frobenius self-conjugacy):** for g = M^2 + t and h = 1, T^2∘φ = φ∘T with φ(u) = (Mu)^2, and periods double exactly. Proposition C′ is the general version for squares. For g = 1+t+t^2, (1+t)^{2^{k+1}-2} has period exactly 2^{k+2}, so there are infinitely many cycles.

**Renormalization lemmas**
- Line and two-point Frobenius certificates turn a finite exact identity Φ^k(P) = P(X^{p^b}) into a proof of divergence.
- Twist transfer: divergence passes from h to every multiple kh with k(0) = 1, and a divergent rational point gives a divergent polynomial orbit of a twisted map.
- Negative lemma N1: for h = 1, every polynomial periodic point has odd-step fraction 1/deg g. So any certificate for h = 1 must use non-polynomial periodic points.

**New divergent systems (GLOBAL is false)**
- g = 1+t^3, h = 1 (`p2_t3`).
- The family g = (1+t)^{2^k+1}, h = 1, every k ≥ 1 (`p2_cube_k`): the orbit of 1 diverges. The case k = 1 is probably known from Matthews.
- The family g = 1+t+t^{2^k+1} with any twist divisible by 1+t+...+t^{2^k} (`p2_tri_k`).
- The zero-drift multiplier 1+t+t^2 with h = (1+t)^2(1+t+t^3) and all its multiples (`p2_crit`).
- Four F_3 degree-2 multipliers with twists (`p3_a` to `p3_d`).
- Two degree-4 F_2 twisted systems (`p2_sq111`, `p2_1034`).
- Matthews–Leigh's g = 1+t^2 is re-proved and extended to every h (`p2_ML`).

**Classification**
- F_2 with deg g ≤ 2 and any h is complete except g = 1+t+t^2 with a twist not divisible by (1+t)^2(1+t+t^3).
- Every (g, h) with deg g ≤ 1 over any F_q has GLOBAL true.
- The degenerate case g(0) = 0 is settled by one-line arguments.

**Integer transfer:** no new integer result. The method depends on G^{p^n} = G(t^{p^n}), which has no integer counterpart.

**Novelty:** checked by short web searches only; the Matthews–Leigh paper itself was not accessible.

Every cycle other than {0},{h} lies in degree < deg h. The only cycles are {0},{h} iff h=(1+t)^a. If a=0, the basin of h is exactly hF_2[t]\{0}.

theorems.name: Theorem A (progression theorem for p-shift maps)
theorems.statement: Let T(n)=(u_r n+v_r)/p on n = r mod p^kappa, with p prime, p not dividing u_r, satisfying (A1) dilation T(pn)=n, (A0) a strongly connected state graph and (IA) a finite initial-accessibility game modulo L_U^2. Every merging class H, including a hypothetical divergent one, meets every progression x mod N with g(x)=g(H) in arbitrarily large members. Here g is the class of (n mod p^(kappa-1), n mod delta) in the move groupoid, and delta is the gcd of the good parts of the commutator translations of loops. g is the finest T-invariant function of n mod M over all M, and an algorithm (certify.py) computes it exactly. Section 7 gives counterexamples when the hypotheses fail.
theorems.novelty: The 3x+1 case belongs to the circle of ideas of Monks-Monks-Monks-Monks, arXiv:1204.3904. I read only the abstract and did not check whether the paper states this form. General theorem, IA game and algorithm: novelty not checked.

theorems.name: Theorem B (complete list of automatic orbit-invariant labels)
theorems.statement: Assume Theorem A applies, the invariant is state-free (a function of n mod d*), and some cycle has a lap with numerator product a>1. Then a finite-valued orbit-invariant label is k-automatic for some k>=2 iff it is constant on g-classes iff it is periodic mod d* iff it is automatic in every base. In particular, the basins of distinct cycles sharing a g-class are automatic in no base. The proof is a kernel-Cobham lemma with a general dilation identity phi(Py)=phi(Ky), taken from T(pn)=n or from a cycle lap. qrB7_c53 shows the expanding-cycle hypothesis is necessary.
theorems.novelty: Generalizes the kernel argument of round2 qrA3_q17 and split5_3 Theorem 2. Novelty not checked.

theorems.name: Theorem C (quantitative sufficiency)
theorems.statement: #(H ∩ P ∩ [1,X]) >> X^sigma for every merging class H and every compatible progression P. sigma comes from an exact rational certificate of a type-weighted ancestor tree (Lemma C1) together with a uniform-word transfer lemma (C2). Certified values include: split5_3 0.42 (round 2 had 0.238), the split_d family 0.974, 3x+d 0.41, 5x+d 0.198, 7x+1 0.15, 9x+1 0.115, split5_1 0.692 and desc_s32_d65 0.772. For m3_a, sigma -> 1 (every 1-eps is achievable). The heuristic caps (5x+1: 0.651, 7x+1: 0.374, 9x+1: 0.258) are evidence only.
theorems.novelty: Tree counting is classical for 3x+1 (Krasikov; Krasikov-Lagarias), but no constants are quoted here. Generic certificates: novelty not checked.

theorems.name: Theorem D (density-zero sufficient sets)
theorems.statement: Let S_T = {n : n = 1 mod p^{floor(loglog n / (2 log L_U))}}. Under Theorem A with a state-free invariant, S_T has density 0, it meets every merging class, and GLOBAL holds iff every element of S_T is eventually periodic. This covers 5x+1, 7x+1, split5_1, split5_3, m3_b and others. The thinning is extremely slow: for 5x+1, S_T contains every integer below about 10^10.9.
theorems.novelty: Monks et al. build sufficient sets of arbitrarily low density for 3x+1. Density zero for these maps: novelty not checked.

theorems.name: Combination of sufficiency with descent
theorems.statement: Proved: sufficiency together with descent within P settles GLOBAL. Two obstructions are also proved. First, for p-shift maps a cylinder descent certificate valid on a progression with p not dividing N is valid everywhere. Second, any forward-invariant set defined by a good modulus is a union of g-classes. No system was found that the combination settles but descent alone does not.

theorems.name: Proposition P (1932 permutation)
theorems.statement: No sufficient progression can exist, because finite cycles meet only finitely many residue classes. What replaces sufficiency: an orbit of the 1932 map (or of any kappa=1 p-shift) is infinite iff it meets at least k+1 classes mod 3^k for every k. The proof combines a complexity argument with the cylinder lemma.

prove:progressions.summary:
Three results here are proved: a general arithmetic-progression theorem for p-shift maps, a theorem listing every automatic orbit-invariant label, and an exponent-counting theorem. Applied to the census, they settle 15 basin questions not previously analysed in the census or by the other round-3 lenses. All five check scripts exit 0, under 2 minutes each.

Theorem A (progression theorem): every merging class, divergent ones included, meets every progression allowed by an explicit invariant g. certify.py computes g exactly, and construct.py runs the proof itself, building an explicit start inside the target progression that merges with the given orbit. The check verified 326 random targets exactly; 4 more were skipped for time, none failed. The algorithm reproduces the earlier results for split5_3, split_5, qrB7_c53 and the split_d family from the concurrent deep lens.

Theorem B (automatic labels): a finite-valued orbit-invariant label is automatic in some base exactly when it is periodic mod d*. qrB7_c53 shows the hypothesis of a cycle with an expanding step is necessary.

The 15 newly answered basin questions:
- m3_a/m3_c: both basins are dense in every progression and automatic in no base.
- desc_s32_d65: the basin of 65 is exactly 65Z; the other seven basins are non-automatic.
- Open systems: 5x+1, 3x-1, 3x+5, 3x+13, 3x+17, 5x+3, 5x+7, 5x+11, split5_1, m3_d, m3_e, m3_g and desc_m3_4n5. In each, known cycles sharing a class have basins that are automatic in no base.

Theorem C (counting): exponents are certified in exact rational arithmetic. split5_3 improves from 0.238 to 0.42; m3_a reaches 1 - eps.

Other results:
- Theorem D gives density-zero sufficient sets. They thin out only above about 10^11 for 5x+1, so the result is qualitative.
- For the 1932 permutation (CLS-040), no sufficient progression can exist. The replacement is proved: an orbit is infinite iff it meets at least k+1 classes mod 3^k for every k.
- The combination question is a negative partial result: two obstructions are proved and no system is settled by it.
- div23_5n1 remains open (evidence only).

Novelty: not checked beyond the Monks et al. abstract.
prove:progressions.open_frontier: Can hypothesis (IA) be dropped from Theorem A? Its conclusion is expected for 3x+3, 5x+5 and 7x+7, but this is not proved here. A two-denominator version (div23_5n1, the q-family in general, farkas5m) needs a lift lemma that does not require infinitely many divisions by each prime. Can first-return descent within a p-adic or U-adic progression be certified anywhere plain descent fails? For the 1932 permutation: does every infinite orbit meet every progression? That is equivalent to every infinite itinerary containing every finite word. For 3x+1-type maps, the certified exponents could be pushed toward 1 with Krasikov-Lagarias-style difference inequalities on top of the type-weight certificates.

referee:progressions.overall:
Theorems A, B, D and Proposition P hold up on re-derivation and on my own check, but four repairs are needed before the lens is done. The arithmetic-progression core (Theorem A) is sound. My from-scratch check (/home/riv/Code/collatz/census/round3/progressions/referee1_check.py, exit 0, about 105 s) found no counterexample:
- At 253 (system, modulus) pairs, the finest invariant computed directly matches the claimed g.
- 92 fresh Theorem A constructions were replayed with my own maps.
- On 102 random maps where Theorem A applies, 292 constructions were replayed.

All five prover checks exit 0, and I showed two of them can fail by mutating their inputs.

Problems found:
- **WRONG:** "no sufficient progression can exist" for the 1932 permutation. The odd numbers are sufficient. Together with all of Z>=1, they are the only sufficient progressions.
- **GAP in Theorem C, Lemma C2:** the construction length grows with the U-valuation of z. This leaves 13 systems' exponents unproved: the split_d family 0.974, split5_1 0.692, d65 0.772, and m3_a sigma->1. A repair route (lemma R) is verified exactly. The other 19 exponents stand, including split5_3 0.42.
- **GAP in Theorem B:** the clause "no automaton separates the basins" is not proved for separators that are not orbit-invariant, and the m3_e sentence about the orbit of 7 is literally false.
- **Novelty:** the 3x+1 case of Theorem A is K. M. Monks, Proc. AMS 134 (2006) 2861-2872, and must be cited. Its source is https://www.ams.org/journals/proc/2006-134-10/S0002-9939-06-08567-4, as confirmed in https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1204.3904.

The full report is /home/riv/Code/collatz/census/round3/progressions/REFEREE1.md.

theorems.statement: The combination lemma is proved. Two obstructions are proved: a cylinder descent certificate on a progression with p not dividing N is already global, and a forward-invariant progression mod a good modulus is a union of g-classes. No system was settled by the combination.

theorems.name: Proposition P0 (1932 permutation: sufficient progressions)
theorems.statement: The sufficient progressions of the 1932 map are exactly Z>=1 and 1 mod 2. T(3q+1) and T(3q+2) are odd and T(3q)=2q<3q, so every orbit contains an odd number. The cycles (1) and (2 3) force N | 2. This replaces the WRONG claim 'no sufficient progression can exist'.

theorems.name: Proposition P (complexity criterion for kappa=1 p-shift maps, e.g. the 1932 map)
theorems.statement: A forward orbit is eventually periodic iff, for some k, it meets at most k classes mod p^k. Hence every infinite 1932 orbit meets at least k+1 classes mod 3^k for every k.
theorems.novelty: A Morse-Hedlund-type argument combined with the cylinder lemma; novelty not checked.

systems.question: Is there a finite-state rule telling the basins of (1) and (2) apart?

systems.answer: The invariant is gcd(n,65). The basin of 65 is exactly 65Z. The other seven basins are non-automatic in every base. Classes {1,7} and {5,1135} are exhausted by their two basins, so no automatic set separates those pairs. sigma = 0.772 (Lemma R).

systems.question: Automatic basin rule; sufficient sets
systems.answer: The invariant is trivial. The basins of 1, 13 and 17 are non-automatic, and no automatic orbit-invariant label separates them. GLOBAL holds iff the eventually-periodic set is automatic. Every progression and S_T are sufficient. sigma = 0.198.

systems.answer: The basins of 1, 5 and 17 are non-automatic in every base (label level).

systems.answer: The invariant is 5|n. The 5 unit cycles have non-automatic basins. The basin of (5 20 10) is automatic iff the Collatz conjecture holds.

systems.answer: The invariant is trivial. The basins of 1 and 13 are non-automatic. Every progression and S_T are sufficient. >> X^0.692 per progression (repaired via Lemma R).

systems.answer: GLOBAL plus 'no other cycle' holds iff the basin of the known cycle is automatic in some base. For 3x+1, the sufficiency input is Monks (2006).

systems.question: What replaces sufficiency?
systems.answer: The only sufficient progressions are Z and 1 mod 2 (Proposition P0; the earlier claim was WRONG and is withdrawn). Every infinite orbit meets at least k+1 classes mod 3^k (Proposition P).
